title: How to Transfer from Dana to OVO: A Simple Guide
summary: Want to transfer from Dana to OVO in Indonesia? Learn the easiest methods, step-by-step tips, and what to know before sending money between e-wallets.
body_markdown:
[Personal Finance](https://blog.transfez.com/en/personal-finance/)


If you have ever stared at your *Dana* balance and wished you could just zap it straight into your *OVO* account, you are definitely not alone. Indonesia’s digital wallet scene is thriving, but the one thing that still trips people up is moving money *between* different platforms. It sounds like it should be simple, right? Yet a surprising number of people end up Googling “how to transfer from Dana to OVO” at 11 PM while trying to split a dinner bill. Sound familiar?


The good news is that it is absolutely doable, and once you know the right method, the whole thing takes just a few minutes. Whether you are[an Indonesian living abroad](https://blog.transfez.com/en/indonesian-diaspora-living-abroad-complete-guide/) who needs to help family manage digital payments back home, or you are right here in Jakarta juggling multiple e-wallets, this guide has you covered.

##


**Why People Want to Transfer from Dana to OVO**


Before diving into the how-to, it helps to understand why this comes up so often. Both *Dana* and *OVO* are two of the biggest digital wallets in Indonesia, but they are used in slightly different contexts. OVO is the go-to for Grab rides and Tokopedia shopping, while Dana has a loyal base for marketplace transactions and everyday QR payments.


Life does not always cooperate with which wallet you happen to have topped up. You might have loaded your Dana account for a bill payment but then realized your friend only accepts OVO. Or you simply want to consolidate your balance in one place. Whatever the reason, moving funds between the two is a real and common need.


###


**1. The Direct Transfer Limitation You Should Know**


Here is the honest truth: **Dana and OVO are not directly linked** to each other. There is no built-in feature inside the Dana app that lets you tap a button and send money straight into an OVO wallet as of now. Both platforms are competitors, so deep native integration between them is not something either company has prioritized.


Do not let this discourage you, though. There is a reliable workaround that most Indonesians use every single day, and it only takes a couple of extra steps.


###


**2. The Bank Transfer Method (The Most Reliable Way)**


The most widely used method to transfer from Dana to OVO is to **route the funds through a bank account** . Here is how it works in practice.


**Step 1: Withdraw from Dana to your bank account.** Open your Dana app, tap the withdraw or transfer option, and select your linked bank account (such as BCA, Mandiri, BNI, BRI, or others). Enter the amount and confirm the transaction.


**Step 2: Top up OVO from your bank account.** Once the funds land in your bank account (this is usually near-instant for most major Indonesian banks), open your OVO app. Select the top-up option, choose your bank, and transfer the desired amount into your OVO balance.


Yes, it is two steps instead of one. But it is **safe, proven, and works every time** . Most people find the whole process takes under five minutes once you have your bank account properly linked to both apps.


###


**3. Using Virtual Account or Bank Transfer Inside OVO**


OVO provides a *virtual account* number for top-ups via bank transfer. This means you can sometimes initiate the transfer directly from your Dana app by using the “bank transfer” feature and entering OVO’s virtual account number as the destination. The steps look like this:


1. In your Dana app, go to “Transfer” and select bank transfer.
2. Choose the bank that OVO’s virtual account is associated with (commonly BNI or others depending on OVO’s current options).
3. Enter the virtual account number provided in your OVO app under the top-up section.
4. Enter the amount and complete the transfer.


This approach can feel more direct because you are initiating everything from Dana without logging into your bank app as a middle step. The catch is that you need to make sure the virtual account details are accurate and up to date inside your OVO app before you start.


###


**4. The GoPay or LinkAja Bridge (Alternative Routes)**


Some users get creative and use a third e-wallet as a bridge if they have one. For instance, if you have a *GoPay* or *LinkAja* account that is connected to both your Dana and OVO flows via a shared bank, you can use it as a stepping stone. This is less common and adds an extra layer of steps, so most people stick with the direct bank method described above. Still, it is good to know this option exists if you are in a pinch.


###


**5. Tips to Make the Process Faster and Smoother**


A few practical pointers that will save you headaches:


- **Link your bank account to both apps in advance.** Do not wait until you urgently need to transfer. Set this up on a calm afternoon so everything is verified and ready to go.
- **Check your daily transfer limits.** Both Dana and OVO have transaction limits that vary depending on your account verification level. Make sure your KTP is verified on both platforms to unlock higher limits.
- **Do transfers during banking hours for faster processing.** While most transfers are near-instant, occasional delays can happen outside of standard banking hours, especially for certain banks.
- **Keep both apps updated.** An outdated app version can sometimes cause unexpected errors during transfers.
- **Save your OVO virtual account number somewhere handy.** If you do this transfer regularly, having the number saved in your contacts or notes app will speed things up considerably.


###


**6. What About Transferring Money Internationally?**


If your situation involves moving money across borders, such as sending funds from overseas into an Indonesian digital wallet, the process is a bit different. E-wallets like Dana and OVO are generally designed for domestic transactions within Indonesia. For international remittances, you would typically need a dedicated international transfer service.


Understanding[what a SWIFT code is](https://blog.transfez.com/en/what-is-a-swift-code-complete-guide/) becomes handy here, since international bank transfers often require one. And if you are looking at how funds move from a foreign account into Indonesia, you might want to read up on[how to transfer money from abroad to Indonesia](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-transfer-money-from-abroad-to-indonesia/) for a broader picture of your options.


##


**Common Questions About Dana to OVO Transfers**


###


**1. Is there a direct Dana to OVO transfer feature?**


Not natively, at least not in the way you might hope. The bank account method remains the standard workaround that works reliably for most users.


###


**2. How long does the transfer take?**


The Dana withdrawal to a bank account is typically instant or within a few minutes for major banks. The OVO top-up from the bank is also usually instant. So end-to-end, you are looking at under five minutes in most cases.


###


**3. Do I need to be fully verified on both apps?**


For smooth transfers, yes. A fully verified account (with your national ID linked) gives you access to higher limits and fewer friction points. If your account is still at the basic level, you may hit low transaction caps quickly.


##


**Wrapping It Up**


Transferring from Dana to OVO in Indonesia is not as seamless as clicking one button, but it is absolutely manageable once you know the steps. The bank account bridge method is your most reliable friend here. Set up your linked accounts ahead of time, verify your identity on both platforms, and you will be moving money between wallets without breaking a sweat.
